name: TrustedRandomAccess
documentation:
An iterator whose items are random-accessible efficiently

 # Safety

 The iterator's `size_hint` must be exact and cheap to call.

 `TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size` may not be overridden.

 All subtypes and all supertypes of `Self` must also implement `TrustedRandomAccess`.
 In particular, this means that types with non-invariant parameters usually can not have
 an impl for `TrustedRandomAccess` that depends on any trait bounds on such parameters, except
 for bounds that come from the respective struct/enum definition itself, or bounds involving
 traits that themselves come with a guarantee similar to this one.

 If `Self: ExactSizeIterator` then `self.len()` must always produce results consistent
 with `self.size()`.

 If `Self: Iterator`, then `<Self as Iterator>::__iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx)`
 must be safe to call provided the following conditions are met.

 1. `0 <= idx` and `idx < self.size()`.
 2. If `Self: !Clone`, then `self.__iterator_get_unchecked(idx)` is never called with the same
    index on `self` more than once.
 3. After `self.__iterator_get_unchecked(idx)` has been called, then `self.next_back()` will
    only be called at most `self.size() - idx - 1` times. If `Self: Clone` and `self` is cloned,
    then this number is calculated for `self` and its clone individually,
    but `self.next_back()` calls that happened before the cloning count for both `self` and the clone.
 4. After `self.__iterator_get_unchecked(idx)` has been called, then only the following methods
    will be called on `self` or on any new clones of `self`:
     * `std::clone::Clone::clone`
     * `std::iter::Iterator::size_hint`
     * `std::iter::DoubleEndedIterator::next_back`
     * `std::iter::ExactSizeIterator::len`
     * `std::iter::Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked`
     * `std::iter::TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size`
 5. If `Self` is a subtype of `T`, then `self` is allowed to be coerced
    to `T`. If `self` is coerced to `T` after `self.__iterator_get_unchecked(idx)` has already
    been called, then no methods except for the ones listed under 4. are allowed to be called
    on the resulting value of type `T`, either. Multiple such coercion steps are allowed.
    Regarding 2. and 3., the number of times `__iterator_get_unchecked(idx)` or `next_back()` is
    called on `self` and the resulting value of type `T` (and on further coercion results with
    super-supertypes) are added together and their sums must not exceed the specified bounds.

 Further, given that these conditions are met, it must guarantee that:

 * It does not change the value returned from `size_hint`
 * It must be safe to call the methods listed above on `self` after calling
   `self.__iterator_get_unchecked(idx)`, assuming that the required traits are implemented.
 * It must also be safe to drop `self` after calling `self.__iterator_get_unchecked(idx)`.
 * If `Self` is a subtype of `T`, then it must be safe to coerce `self` to `T`.
rules: Implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must ensure that the iterator's size_hint is exact.
Implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must ensure that the iterator's size_hint is cheap to call.
Implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must not override TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size.

All subtypes and all supertypes of Self must also implement TrustedRandomAccess. In particular, implementations for types with non-invariant parameters usually cannot depend on trait bounds on those parameters, except bounds from the respective struct/enum definition or bounds involving traits with a similar subtype/supertype implementation guarantee.
If Self: ExactSizeIterator, self.len() must always produce results consistent with self.size().

If Self: Iterator, implementors must ensure that <Self as Iterator>::__iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx) is safe to call when all of these conditions hold: 0 <= idx < self.size(); if Self: !Clone, the same index is never used more than once on self; after the call, next_back() is called at most self.size() - idx - 1 times, with this limit calculated individually for self and each clone when Self: Clone, but with next_back() calls before cloning counting for both; after the call, only Clone::clone, Iterator::size_hint, DoubleEndedIterator::next_back, ExactSizeIterator::len, Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked, and TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size are called on self or any new clones. Coercion from Self to a supertype T, including multiple successive coercions, is permitted; after an unchecked access, the same method restriction applies to every resulting value, and unchecked-access counts for each index and next_back() counts are added across self and all successive coercion results and must remain within the stated bounds.

If Self: Iterator, __iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx) must not change the value returned by size_hint when all of these conditions hold: 0 <= idx < self.size(); if Self: !Clone, the same index is never used more than once on self; after the call, next_back() is called at most self.size() - idx - 1 times, with this limit calculated individually for self and each clone when Self: Clone, but with next_back() calls before cloning counting for both; after the call, only Clone::clone, Iterator::size_hint, DoubleEndedIterator::next_back, ExactSizeIterator::len, Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked, and TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size are called on self or any new clones. Coercion from Self to a supertype T, including multiple successive coercions, is permitted; after an unchecked access, the same method restriction applies to every resulting value, and unchecked-access counts for each index and next_back() counts are added across self and all successive coercion results and must remain within the stated bounds.

If Self: Iterator, after __iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx), it must be safe to call Clone::clone, Iterator::size_hint, DoubleEndedIterator::next_back, ExactSizeIterator::len, Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked, and TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size on self, assuming their required traits are implemented, when all of these conditions hold: 0 <= idx < self.size(); if Self: !Clone, the same index is never used more than once on self; after the unchecked call, next_back() is called at most self.size() - idx - 1 times, with this limit calculated individually for self and each clone when Self: Clone, but with next_back() calls before cloning counting for both; after the unchecked call, only those six methods are called on self or any new clones. Coercion from Self to a supertype T, including multiple successive coercions, is permitted; after an unchecked access, the same method restriction applies to every resulting value, and unchecked-access counts for each index and next_back() counts are added across self and all successive coercion results and must remain within the stated bounds.

If Self: Iterator, it must be safe to drop self after __iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx) when all of these conditions hold: 0 <= idx < self.size(); if Self: !Clone, the same index is never used more than once on self; after the call, next_back() is called at most self.size() - idx - 1 times, with this limit calculated individually for self and each clone when Self: Clone, but with next_back() calls before cloning counting for both; after the call, only Clone::clone, Iterator::size_hint, DoubleEndedIterator::next_back, ExactSizeIterator::len, Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked, and TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size are called on self or any new clones. Coercion from Self to a supertype T, including multiple successive coercions, is permitted; after an unchecked access, the same method restriction applies to every resulting value, and unchecked-access counts for each index and next_back() counts are added across self and all successive coercion results and must remain within the stated bounds.

If Self: Iterator and Self is a subtype of T, it must be safe to coerce self to T after __iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx) when all of these conditions hold: 0 <= idx < self.size(); if Self: !Clone, the same index is never used more than once on self; after the call, next_back() is called at most self.size() - idx - 1 times, with this limit calculated individually for self and each clone when Self: Clone, but with next_back() calls before cloning counting for both; after the call, only Clone::clone, Iterator::size_hint, DoubleEndedIterator::next_back, ExactSizeIterator::len, Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked, and TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size are called on self or any new clones. Multiple successive coercions to supertypes are permitted; after an unchecked access, the same method restriction applies to every resulting value, and unchecked-access counts for each index and next_back() counts are added across self and all successive coercion results and must remain within the stated bounds.
